subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
SCOPE AND STANDING. This BOUNDS claim.law.declaration-order-numbers-the-registers-assignment-order-schedules-the-loads.20260901.v1. That law is correct but under-specified: declaration order numbers the callee-saved registers only WITHIN a group, and there are two groups, whose membership is decided ahead of the declaration sequence itself.

THE RULE. MWCC assigns callee-saved GPRs downward from r31 in two passes. FIRST pass: locals that carry an initializer at their declaration, in declaration order. SECOND pass: locals declared without an initializer, in declaration order. A local in the second group therefore colours BELOW every local in the first group no matter how early it is declared. Measured on show_piles, whose declaration order is tbl, blit(uninit), pl, adj(init), result(init): `blit` is the SECOND thing declared and still received the LOWEST of the three (r29), while adj (4th) and result (5th) took r31 and r30 in their own declaration order. Moving `result`'s declaration from 5th to 3rd -- still behind blit, still inside the initialized group -- lifted it r30 -> r31 and pushed adj r31 -> r30, matching target on adj and improving real 60 -> 58 with the instruction count and opcode multiset untouched. So position governs, but only after group membership does.

COROLLARY 1, A DEAD INITIALIZER DOES NOT PROMOTE. Group membership is decided AFTER dead-store elimination, not from the syntax. Spelling the uninitialized local `u8* blit = 0;` -- a real initializer, syntactically in the first group -- measured byte-for-byte NEUTRAL: MWCC strips an initializer whose value is overwritten before any use, and the local stays in the second group. You cannot buy a higher register with an initializer the compiler will not keep. This is the mirror of claim.law.noop-cast-on-array-decay-not-neutral.20260831.v1: there the cast NODE was load-bearing though the resulting type was not; here the initializer node is NOT load-bearing once its value is dead.

COROLLARY 2, DEMOTION COSTS MORE THAN PROMOTION PAYS -- DO NOT INVERT THE GROUPS TO CHASE A NUMBER. The obvious constructive cure, moving the initialized locals into the uninitialized group so an early-declared pointer can reach r31, is a NET LOSS and was measured twice. Making adj and result uninitialized and assigning them as statements did put all three in one group in declaration order, but regressed real 58 -> 66; splitting the `counts` pointer's declaration from its assignment the same way regressed real 60 -> 68. The mechanism is the same both times and is worth naming on its own: an initializer at the declaration PINS the value's computation inside the declaration block, and converting it to a statement lets MWCC sink the whole dependence chain below the `stmw` frame store, dragging every chain that shares a base or a global load with it. Register numbering is a cheap lever; assignment-form is an expensive one, and they are the same edit seen from two sides.

THE SCREEN, before spending a build. If the local you want to promote is only ASSIGNED after a loop or a call, its register is not reachable through declaration form at all: classify the residual source-unreachable and stop probing it. If it is initialized at its declaration, reposition it within the initialized group and expect the move to be worth roughly one register per position.

MEASUREMENT NOTE. All five probes held the instruction count at 102/102 and the opcode multiset at IDENTICAL, so `real` was the only moving instrument and no metric arbitration was needed. On a function that is NOT already count-exact this axis will be confounded, exactly as claim.law.record-respelling-pays-per-region-not-per-population.20260901.v1 Corollary 1 warns.
